items.title: When the ideal is the whole ring the glued category is equivalent to the category of modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a flat ring map and an ideal generated by finitely many elements whose ideal is the whole ring, the functor sending a module to its glued object and the functor sending a glued object to its global sections are quasi-inverse equivalences between modules and the glued category (statement lines 24767-24774). The proof takes an arbitrary glued object, uses the glueing statement for modules over a flat cover to produce a module realizing its localizations, identifies the cover component of the object with the base change of that module by comparing their localizations at the elements, and combines the resulting essential image statement with the known composite to conclude (proof lines 24776-24788). The comparison of the two cover components through their localizations is what makes the argument work in this degenerate case where the ideal is the whole ring. The counted span refers twice, once to a result of another chapter and once to an earlier result of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-equivalence-I-unit (canonical tag 05EP), with the displayed equivalence of categories (source lines 24767-24774)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the glueing of a module out of the given data by the algebra statement, the observation that both components are modules over the flat cover recovering the same localizations and hence canonically isomorphic, and the conclusion that the object lies in the essential image, combined with the earlier statement that one composite is the identity (source lines 24776-24789)
